title: Min Cost Climbing Stairs
keyIdea: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i − 1], dp[i − 2]) is the cheapest total to stand on step i. Start on step 0 or 1; the top is reached from the last two steps: answer = min(dp[n − 1], dp[n − 2]). Two variables give O(1) space.

approaches.name: Plain recursion
approaches.why: Each call branches twice and the same subproblems are solved again and again.

approaches.name: Memoization (top-down)
approaches.idea: Same recursion, caching each step's answer in dp.

approaches.name: Your tabulation (bottom-up array)
approaches.idea: dp[0] = cost[0], dp[1] = cost[1]; dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i − 1], dp[i − 2]).
approaches.why: One pass, but keeps the whole dp array.

approaches.name: Two variables
approaches.idea: Same recurrence keeping only prev2 and prev1.
approaches.why: Only the last two values are ever read.

options: The cheapest total cost to stand on step i, having paid cost[i]
The cost to reach the top

quiz.q: Why is the answer min(dp[n − 1], dp[n − 2])?
options: The top is one jump past the end, reachable from either of the last two steps

quiz.q: Why do steps 0 and 1 start at their own cost?
options: You may start on either one directly, paying only that step

quiz.q: How does the space go from O(n) to O(1)?
options: Only dp[i − 1] and dp[i − 2] are read, so keep two variables
